newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Red chip fever grips Hong Kong before China takeover.
newsitem.headline: Red chip fever grips Hong Kong before China takeover.

text.p: A feeding frenzy for China related stocks has reached fever pitch during Hong Kong's final weeks of British rule, with thousands of punters flocking to banks for a second day in a row to snap up the offerings.
The latest "red chip" stock to be listed in an initial public offering, Beijing Enterprise Holdings Ltd, was drawing unprecedented demand from retail investors, market sources said on Wednesday.

For the second day in a row banks ran out of application forms. "We have never seen retail interest at this level before," said Tom Grimmer, a spokesman for Peregrine Capital Ltd, one of the global coordinators of the issue.

Beijing Enterprises' IPO comes amid a heady craze for red chip stocks in Hong Kong. Red chips -- Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from mainland China -- have been a dominant investment theme in the stock market as Hong Kong prepares to return to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
"I suspect that the China enthusiasm will only intensify," said Robert Rountree, regional strategist at Nomura Research Institute (Hong Kong) Ltd.
"It is very clear that China has turned the economic cycle. You have got very low inflation and economic growth is starting to pick up again."
Hong Kong residents are well known for their appetite for making a quick buck - whether it be in the property market, on the race course or in the stock market.

Beijing Enterprises is expected to be a star performer on the Hong Kong stock market since it is controlled by the Beijing municipal government which is expected to inject valuable assets into the company at attractive prices.
Beijing Enterprises owns a stake in Beijing McDonald's, the company which operates the fast-food chain in the city. It also has interests in brewing, toll roads, hotels and retailing.
The company is offering 150 million shares in a global flotation at HK$12.48 per share. Ten percent is being offered to the Hong Kong public and 90 percent to international investors.

Peregrine said several thousand people tried to cram into its Hong Kong offices on Tuesday to subscribe to the issue, forcing the investment house to set up a special office on Wednesday to deal with the crowds.
"This is definitely momentum investing -- a euphoric fever that grips the market so often," said Peter Churchouse, regional strategist at Morgan Stanley.
"It is like the property market late last year and early this year. It gets this frenzy going that feeds on itself and valuation and rational analysis goes out the window."

An initial 400,000 applications forms for Beijing Enterprises' Hong Kong offering were swept up by investors on the first subscription day on Tuesday and local newspapers said people were selling the forms for HK$100.
A further 500,000 forms were printed overnight but were soon exhausted.
"Banks have run out," a source close to the underwriters said on Wednesday.

Peregrine has asked for another 200,000 forms to be printed. The deadline for applications to subscribe to the issue is on Friday and the Hong Kong offering is expected to be more than 1,000 times subscribed, the highest ever in the territory.
